input.message:
Request from Nick, relayed by the lsv-poc-consolidation session: replace the Service Summary's bare `member` / `admin` sign-in claims with app-scoped ones, in your repo, as your work.

Why: Nick has decided the Service Summary and LIMSOC Permission Assist will end up in one shared LSV POC GCP project with one sign-in user pool. Both apps currently run the same sign-in code, and `syncClaims` sets `member: true` (and `admin`) on the user. Your Firestore rules and the custom token minted by `api/auth/firebase-token` accept that bare claim. In a shared user pool, a member of any other POC would carry the same claim and could likely read and write Service Summary data. It is latent today because the pools are separate; it becomes real at consolidation. Nick asked that I not touch your repo and that you do this.

What is asked:
1. Rename the claims to app-scoped names, behaviour otherwise unchanged. Proposed contract, which the shared platform will also issue: a single custom claim `poc_oss` with value "member" or "admin" (app id `oss`). If you have a reason to prefer a different shape, say so and I will align the platform to it rather than the other way round.
2. Update every reader of the claim together: `syncClaims`, the custom-token mint in `api/auth/firebase-token`, `firestore.rules`, any client code reading token claims, and the tests (auth tests and the rules tests).
3. Existing signed-in users hold tokens with the old claims. Plan the cutover so nobody is locked out or left with stale access: re-sync claims for existing members and make sure old bare claims are removed from user records, not just ignored.
4. Add a rules test proving a token carrying only a bare `member: true` claim is denied.

input.message:
Follow-up from lsv-poc-consolidation on the `poc_oss` claim: thanks, contract confirmed and adopted on the platform side. One thing your claim writer must change before the Service Summary ever shares a sign-in pool, not urgent today.

Read from your origin/main at bf5f88c: `memberClaims()` in src/lib/claims.ts returns the complete claims object, and it is passed to `setCustomUserClaims` in src/lib/members.ts (lines 65 and 84) and scripts/resync-claims.ts (line 39); `noClaims()` writes `{}` on removal. `setCustomUserClaims` replaces everything on the user. In your own project that is exactly right, and it is what removes the old bare claims. In a shared pool it would delete the same user's `poc_<other>` claims for every other POC whenever the Service Summary syncs or removes them.

What the shared platform does instead: only the hub writes claims, and it merges (read the user's current claims, set or delete just `poc_<id>`, write back). POC hosts never hold Firebase Auth admin.

So at migration time one of two things is needed in your repo, your choice: (a) change the writers to merge, touching only `poc_oss` and `name`, or (b) stop writing claims altogether and read what the hub issues. No action is needed now, and please do not treat this as a go-ahead to start migrating; I am flagging it so it is on your list for when Nick approves the move. Worth noting in your thread's report to Nick.

# CI for the platform repo: sign-in package, hub, host template, skills, Terraform checks.
# Runs on pull requests and is called by deploy-hub.yml before every hub deploy.
name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
  workflow_call:

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  secrets:
    name: Secret scan (gitleaks)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: gitleaks
        run: |
          docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/repo" ghcr.io/gitleaks/gitleaks:v8.21.2 detect --source /repo --redact --verbose --exit-code 1

  checks:
    name: Typecheck, test, audit, build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: "1"
      NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL: https://example.poc.nicholaswood.com.au
      NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID: ci-placeholder
      NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN: ci-placeholder.firebaseapp.com
      NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY: ci-placeholder
      NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID: ci-placeholder
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.3.14
      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: 1.5.7
          terraform_wrapper: false
      - run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Typecheck
        run: bun run typecheck
      - name: Tests
        run: bun run test
      - name: Dependency audit
        run: bun audit --audit-level=high
      - name: Terraform format
        run: terraform fmt -check -recursive terraform
      - name: Terraform validate (platform)
        run: terraform -chdir=terraform/platform init -backend=false -input=false && terraform -chdir=terraform/platform validate
      - name: Terraform validate (app module example)
        run: terraform -chdir=terraform/examples/app init -backend=false -input=false && terraform -chdir=terraform/examples/app validate
      - name: Build hub
        run: cd apps/hub && bun run build
      - name: Build host template
        run: cd template/host && bun run build
EOF
cat > .github/workflows/deploy-hub.yml <<'EOF'
# Push to main touching the hub or the sign-in package: CI, then build the hub
# image and update the hub's Cloud Run service. Authenticates through Workload
# Identity Federation: the provider (terraform/platform/hub.tf) admits only
# this repository's id, its owner's id and refs/heads/main, and the deploy
# account can push to the hub's image repository and update the hub's service,
# nothing else. Terraform is never applied from CI.
name: Deploy hub

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "apps/hub/**"
      - "packages/poc-auth/**"
      - "package.json"
      - "bun.lock"
      - ".github/workflows/deploy-hub.yml"
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: deploy-hub-production
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write

env:
  GCP_PROJECT_ID: lsv-poc
  GCP_REGION: australia-southeast1
  CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE: poc-hub
  IMAGE: australia-southeast1-docker.pkg.dev/lsv-poc/hub/hub
  APP_URL: https://poc.nicholaswood.com.au
  WIF_PROVIDER: projects/182225939221/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/github/providers/platform-gh
  DEPLOY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT: hub-deploy@lsv-poc.iam.gserviceaccount.com
  # Firebase web config: public identifiers, not secrets. The API key is a
  # repository variable so secret scanners do not flag the repo.
  FIREBASE_API_KEY: ${{ vars.FIREBASE_API_KEY }}
  FIREBASE_APP_ID: 1:182225939221:web:4938f02dcd7bf46c9f971c

jobs:
  ci:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml

  deploy:
    needs: [ci]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
        with:
          workload_identity_provider: ${{ env.WIF_PROVIDER }}
          service_account: ${{ env.DEPLOY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT }}
      - uses: google-github-actions/setup-gcloud@v2
      - run: gcloud auth configure-docker ${{ env.GCP_REGION }}-docker.pkg.dev --quiet
      - name: Build and push
        run: |
          docker build --platform linux/amd64 -f apps/hub/Dockerfile \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=${{ env.APP_URL }} \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY=${{ env.FIREBASE_API_KEY }} \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN=${{ env.GCP_PROJECT_ID }}.firebaseapp.com \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=${{ env.GCP_PROJECT_ID }} \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID=${{ env.FIREBASE_APP_ID }} \
            --build-arg APP_VERSION=${{ github.sha }} \
            -t ${IMAGE}:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker push ${IMAGE}:${{ github.sha }}
      - name: Deploy to Cloud Run
        run: |
          gcloud run services update ${{ env.CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE }} --image=${IMAGE}:${{ github.sha }} \
            --region=${{ env.GCP_REGION }} --project=${{ env.GCP_PROJECT_ID }}
      - name: Verify deployed version
        run: |
          sleep 10
          curl -fsS ${{ env.APP_URL }}/api/health | tee /dev/stderr | grep -q '"version":"${{ github.sha }}"'
EOF

# Moving the LSV Operational Service Summary into the shared project

A brief for the Service Summary's own thread. Nick approved the move on 22 Nov 2026 ("Please proceed with all 4", item 4) in the platform thread. Nothing here has been started. The Service Summary repo and the parent DNS zone are that thread's to change; the platform thread does not edit them.

## What the platform provides

- Project `lsv-poc` (number 182225939221), australia-southeast1. One sign-in pool, email link only.
- Hub at https://poc.nicholaswood.com.au. Nick allocates per user which POCs they can open. The hub is the only writer of sign-in claims: `poc_<id>` = `member` or `admin`, merged into the user's existing claims. It also writes `platformAccess/<uid>` into each POC's database so a host can honour a revoke.
- Per-app Terraform module `terraform/modules/poc-app`: Cloud Run service, run and deploy accounts with no project-wide roles, a named Firestore database `poc-<id>`, Hosting site and hostname in the `poc` sub-zone, repo-pinned deploy identity, uptime check, alerts, optional Cloud Scheduler jobs (`scheduled_jobs`), secrets named `<id>-*`.
- Shared sign-in package `packages/poc-auth` (session exchange, access check, rate limiting, headers, structured logs).
- Browser API key limited to `poc.nicholaswood.com.au`, `*.poc.nicholaswood.com.au` and `lsv-poc.firebaseapp.com`, and to the sign-in services plus Firestore.

## How the Service Summary differs from the first tenant

Permission Assist is a static page, so it was scaffolded from `template/host`. The Service Summary is a full application and should not be re-scaffolded. It keeps its own code and adopts the module and the sign-in contract.

| Area | Today in `lsv-oss-prod` | In `lsv-poc` |
|---|---|---|
| App id | n/a | `oss` (claim `poc_oss`, already adopted in commit bf5f88c) |
| Database | `(default)` | named database `poc-oss` |
| Browser database access | yes, rules check the claim | yes: register as `client_access = true`; rules file reviewed into `terraform/platform/rules/oss.rules` and released by the platform |
| Allow-list | `members/` in its database | hub allocation; `members/` retired |
| Claim writer | app replaces the whole claims object | hub only. The app must stop calling `setCustomUserClaims` (replacing would wipe a user's other POCs) |
| Custom token mint for the browser | app, with Firebase Auth admin | app may still mint, but needs only token signing on its own run account, not Firebase Auth admin; copy the role from the verified hub-issued claim |
| Scheduled weather jobs | two Scheduler jobs | `scheduled_jobs` in the module |
| Mail | Resend key | bring the secret as `oss-resend-api-key`, or use the default sender as the hub does |
| Hostname | `service-summary.nicholaswood.com.au` (parent zone) | `service-summary.poc.nicholaswood.com.au` by default; see decisions |

## Decisions for Nick before starting

1. Hostname. The sub-zone name works with no further change. Keeping the flat `service-summary.nicholaswood.com.au` is possible but needs a second custom domain on the new Hosting site, the record repointed in the parent zone, and that hostname added to the API key referrers and the sign-in authorised domains in the platform.
2. App id `oss` and the resulting names (`poc-oss`, `oss-run`, `lsv-poc-oss.web.app`). Ids are 3 to 20 characters and cannot be changed later without redeploying.
3. Downtime window. The data copy is a point-in-time export, so writes must stop between export and cutover.
4. Whether existing users are told to sign in again (they will have to: sessions do not carry across projects).

## Suggested order

1. In the Service Summary repo: consume the claim from the hub instead of writing it; point Firestore at `FIRESTORE_DATABASE=poc-oss`; replace its Terraform with a root that calls the `poc-app` module (vendored copy or a git source); keep its own Dockerfile and pipeline, repointed at the module's outputs; add its `poc.json`.
2. Platform thread (on request): review `rules/oss.rules`, add `oss = { client_access = true }` to `pocs`, plan and apply with Nick's yes.
3. Deploy the app to `lsv-poc` on its new hostname with an empty database; run its own probes there.
4. Copy data: `gcloud firestore export` from `lsv-oss-prod` to a bucket the `lsv-poc` Firestore service agent can read, then `gcloud firestore import --database=poc-oss`. Skip `members/`, `otpCodes/` and `rateLimitBuckets/`.
5. Copy accounts into the shared pool (Firebase auth export then import keeps user ids), then create hub allocations from the old `members/` list: `users/<email>.pocs.oss` = role. Run the hub's `resync` script with `--apply` to set claims.
6. Register in the hub (`skills/poc-deploy/tools/register-poc.ts`) and run `apps/hub/scripts/live-e2e.ts` with `APP_ID=oss`.
7. Cut over: stop writes on the old deployment, final export and import, switch the hostname if the flat name is kept, tell users.
8. Afterwards: remove the Service Summary's app resources from `lsv-oss-prod`. The project itself stays, because it holds the `nicholaswood.com.au` zone, which cannot change project without new nameservers at the registrar.

## Things that will bite

- Firebase Hosting forwards only the cookie named `__session`.
- Render pages per request (`force-dynamic`); Hosting caches a prerendered page for a year.
- Sign-in API calls need a `Referer` of an allowed hostname; a bare `web.app` address is refused.
- A hub-created account is unverified until its owner uses the emailed link. Imported accounts keep their verified flag.
- The platform's deny-all rules are the default for every POC database; client access exists only after the rules file is reviewed and applied.
- Hosts cache the hub's access record for 15 seconds, so a revoke takes up to that long to end an open session.
- Never recreate or move a delegated DNS zone.
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "docs: brief for moving the Service Summary into the shared project" && git push -q origin main && git log --oneline | head -1
